Subject: Medallion MAP & evaluation timeline — AWS marketplace purchase path

Hi Elena / Rajesh,

Thanks again for the time today. Per our conversation I’m sharing an initial mutual action plan (MAP) and a suggested evaluation/close timeline for the AWS Marketplace private offer. The goal here is to give your procurement team a clear set of milestones so we can align the technical acceptance, PO, and billing path without surprises.

High-level proposal (attached: Medallion_MAP_v1.xlsx):
- Week 0 (today) — Kickoff: confirm procurement owner and legal reviewer; Redwood sends PO template and map.
- Week 1 — Eval: trial work + acceptance criteria (sample throughput, latency verification).
- Week 2 — Security evidence handoff (SOC2, IP controls) + outstanding questionnaire responses.
- Week 3 — Procurement: PO issuance (AWS Marketplace private offer preferred) and DocuSign signature.
- Week 4 — Billing & activation: private-offer activation and initial invoice / billing path confirmed.

Two billing paths to consider (we can support either):
1) AWS Marketplace private offer (preferred for many enterprise customers): PO issued to AWS, invoice flows through Marketplace; requires coordination with your procurement for Marketplace onboarding.
2) Direct Redwood invoice (vendor invoice): Redwood issues invoice directly to your finance team; we can transition to Marketplace listing post-commit.

Please confirm the right procurement contact (it sounded like Emily Park on your side) and whether Medallion has a preferred billing cadence (Net-30 vs Net-45). I’ve attached a Redwood PO template and the MAP spreadsheet so you can add internal milestones.

Attachments: Medallion_MAP_v1.xlsx, Redwood_PO_Template.docx

If useful I can schedule a quick 20–30 min call with procurement to walk the MAP and the two billing paths.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole

Marissa —

Appreciate the clear summary and the MAP. A few quick clarifications from procurement:
- Procurement owner: Emily Park (cc’d on this thread).
- Billing preference: Our default is Marketplace where possible, but legal needs to confirm that AWS Marketplace invoices satisfy our corporate PO and tax requirements. Net-30 is typical for us.
- Security: we need an up-to-date SOC 2 Type II and a short answers version of the procurement questionnaire attached (see Medallion_Procurement_Questionnaire.pdf).

Two asks: can you confirm whether the private-offer flow will allow us to receive a vendor invoice that ties to our PO for accounting (some marketplaces require AWS to invoice)? Also can you share a rough timeline for acceptance testing (what are the minimal pass/fail criteria for Week 1)?

Hi Rajesh / Elena —

Thanks — answering inline and attaching an updated MAP with explicit acceptance criteria (Medallion_MAP_v1_updated.xlsx) plus our SOC2 report.

1) Billing / private-offer flow:
- AWS private offer typically results in AWS invoicing (Marketplace billing) when the customer chooses that path. That can complicate vendor-invoice reconciliation for some teams.
- For customers that require Redwood-native invoicing tied directly to a Redwood PO, we offer a direct-invoice path as an alternate. That path is functionally identical for service delivery but requires a short commercial exception (we’ll license via Redwood contract rather than the Marketplace ordering flow).
- Recommendation: if your AP prefers Marketplace (and legal confirms), choose Marketplace private offer; if you need Redwood on the invoice, we can do direct invoicing and later migrate to Marketplace.

2) Acceptance criteria (proposed for Week 1 — included in updated MAP):
- Latency: 95th percentile < 220 ms for the sample prompts provided.
- Throughput: sustained 200 tokens/sec across the sample batch size.
- Functional: model returns correct structured output for the three golden prompts in the eval set.
- Security: no PII leakage observed in sample prompts / KV caching test.

3) Timeline: updated sheet includes a 3-week sprint-to-commit option (kickoff -> eval -> procurement -> PO -> activation).

Attachments: Medallion_MAP_v1_updated.xlsx, SOC2_TypeII_report_redwood.pdf

Next steps:
- Rajesh: confirm whether Emily can sign the PO or if another approver is needed.
- Elena: if Marketplace is preferred, confirm and we’ll prepare the private offer paperwork (DocuSign link to follow).
- Ben / Grace: looping you both for any finance/legal flags on the two invoice paths. Ben — can you confirm whether we can accept a Net-30 Redwood vendor invoice as a permanent option if Medallion prefers that?

I’m happy to set a 20-min call tomorrow to walk procurement through the MAP — propose Wed 16 Jul 3pm PT or Thu 17 Jul 9am PT.

Best,
